subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a shared media-core/plugin-safe filename decoder now, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/71517 be refreshed around that boundary or left aside?
rationale: Current code proves the gap remains, but the durable fix changes a shared media/plugin boundary and must decide whether this becomes a generic contract rather than another Feishu-local repair.

options.title: Sponsor shared media-core decoder
options.body: Refresh or replace the candidate with a narrow media-core decoder used by remote media and Feishu paths, with tests for charset labels, mojibake recovery, and Latin-1 passthrough.

options.title: Keep only local channel fixes
options.body: Leave this issue open but limit near-term work to individual Feishu/channel bugs until maintainers want a shared decoder contract.

options.title: Close the candidate PR, keep the issue
options.body: If the current branch is not worth adopting, close the stale candidate PR while keeping this canonical issue for a future boundary-approved implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor shared media-core decoder
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the candidate with a narrow media-core decoder used by remote media and Feishu paths, with tests for charset labels, mojibake recovery, and Latin-1 passthrough.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history on Feishu filename recovery and adjacent media helper work.
